Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_AUTOEXPLOR: Bibi, I keep having to revisit areas I've already cleared... Do I really have to jump in myself every single time? My legs are going to retire before I do.
That's what Auto Explore is for. Once you've cleared an area with at least 1 star, you can earn rewards over time without running the battle yourself.
Oh! So while I'm taking it easy, monster kills, experience, and items can still come in little by little?

Exactly. Depending on your equipped weapon, you gain melee, ranged, or magic exploration experience, and resource areas grant gathering experience based on the resource type. Item rewards are limited by your exploration reward slots.
So how exactly do stars make Auto Explore faster? My perfect clears are finally paying off!

Right? Your effort to get those 3 stars is finally paying off! At 1 star, it takes a whopping 1.5 times the 2-star time limit. But once you hit 2 or 3 stars, that multiplier drops significantly to just 1.2 times their respective limits! The final time displayed at the bottom of the window shows the perfect result after factoring in these multipliers and rounding it off, so go check it out!
But what if I go on a normal exploration while Auto Explore is running? Running both at the same time would be an amazing deal, wouldn't it?
Don't try to get rewards that easily. Auto Explore pauses during normal exploration, and time that passes during normal exploration is not counted toward Auto Explore rewards.
Then what about while the game is closed? I'd love it if the explorers kept working while I sleep!
Yes. When you return to the game by pressing Start Game from the title screen, your offline Auto Explore rewards will be calculated.
Got it. So I should keep enough reward slots open and make sure I still meet the area's requirements!

Correct. Area requirements are checked every time Auto Explore starts. If you fail to meet them, it stops, and if that happens during offline calculation, the summary window will show the reason, so check your materials and required gear carefully.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_BREWING_00: I need some potions that could help with exploration or crafting. Maybe I should take some time to brew them myself.
Good idea. Drinking potions you make yourself can give you powerful skill bonus effects. And depending on the potion's type or grade, the duration can vary.
Oh, so each potion lasts for a different amount of time? Then what happens if I drink several different kinds at once? Do the old effects get overwritten?
Heh, don't worry. Different categories of potions don't overwrite each other—they all stack! And if you keep drinking the same potion, its duration keeps stacking too.
I see! Then I should chug all kinds of potions depending on the situation and stack as many buffs as possible. And if my base stats permanently increase every time I brew one, that's a total win-win!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_CAMPING_00: Um... Bibi, who is that squirrel-tailed girl studying a map so seriously beside the campfire? Her aura is no joke.
Oh, you mean Pori? She's a camping expert. At least, nobody argues with Pori when it comes to choosing a place to sleep.
Ding-ding-ding! But remember this. A clearing drawn too perfectly on a map is nothing but bait from the 'moon cartographers'.
Moon cartographers...? (scared) Why did the mood suddenly get like this?
Shh, we can talk details after we survive. First rule! Before camping, craft your 'camping supplies' first!
You can't spend a night in the wild empty-handed, after all.
Once you use supplies made with care, even the way you move the next day will feel different. You'll experience magic that makes proficiency rise in leaps and bounds.
So camping creates synergy for other activities like cooking and farming?
Exactly! But if a buff is already active, don't forget that only the stronger one stays. A campfire cannot burn its own body, after all.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_CAMPING_01: Also, if you bring Pori what she needs, she'll trade it for useful goods.
What does Pori collect? Don't tell me it's acorns?
No, purple pine cones! I need them to keep the forest fairies from rummaging around inside my head!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_CARTOGRAPH: Every time I head out to explore, I get confused by the paths and waste time... and it's dangerous not knowing where monsters might jump out from.
That's why smart adventurers use the Cartography skill. You spend time carefully drawing and recording maps of the areas you explore.
If I draw a map, can I see confusing routes more clearly and even unlock hidden new paths?

Exactly! Completing a map lets you move into new areas that were previously blocked off. And if you keep mapping places you've already unlocked, your Cartography skill experience rises much faster too.
Ah, I get it! First I should open up new routes, then keep refining maps in unlocked areas to level the skill up in no time. I'd better grab my parchment and quill right away!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_CHALLENGE_: Bibi, I can feel something ominous from that tower and labyrinth. They do not let just anyone enter, do they?
Sharp as ever. The way opens only to adventurers who have trained Endurance to the fifteenth rank. Choose between the Trial Tower and the Rewinding Labyrinth.
A trial tower... I suppose I have to climb patiently from the bottom?
Exactly. You may face only the floor just beyond the highest one you have conquered. Break through to the end, and the floor and its Cycle Stones are yours.
Surely I do not have to fight my way through a conquered floor every single time?
Pay some gold and the keepers will deliver that floor's reward without another battle. It still uses one of the tower's allowances for the day.
Each labyrinth guardian offers three paths: Novice, Adept, and Elite. Can I choose Elite first?
Do not get greedy. Victory on one path opens the next. Bring the Endurance that guardian demands, and defeat it before time runs out.
It seems the tower and labyrinth grant their chances separately. What if I lose or retreat?
A chance is spent only when you win or claim a reward without fighting. Defeat and retreat do not count. The record by the entrance tells you what remains and when it will be restored.
Then I can pay gold to claim rewards from a labyrinth path I have already beaten too?
Correct. The tower yields Cycle Stones, and the labyrinth yields Rewind Thread. Save them to trade for rare goods at the exchange.
But while I am fighting here, does the expedition I entrusted to others keep moving?
It rests while you fight. Once you return here, it continues from where it stopped, so keep your eyes on the foe before you!
Wait, when I fall back during an expedition, I am preparing to leave the fight. Does retreating here mean giving up the challenge too?
No. Battles here work a little differently from expeditions. Retreat only stops your attacks and puts some distance between you and the enemy. Advance when you are ready to face the enemy again!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_COMMERCE_0: I sold all the odds and ends I got from hunting monsters to the shop, and they paid me way less than I expected... This is so unfair!
Tsk, tsk. How naive. If you want a better chance of selling things for their proper value and turning a profit, you need to raise your Commerce skill and sharpen your business sense!
Oh, so if I level up Commerce, I can simply sell items to shops for a higher price right away?
That's not all. You can also spend time negotiating for extra money, or sell items in exchange for a special currency called Ducarin that can be used in special shops.
Oh! Then I can clear out all the junk piling up in my bag efficiently and earn valuable special currency too. I'd better go do some business right now!
Also, use Commodity Trade to buy/sell goods with Ducarin (resets Sat. 21:00). Prices shift based on trading volume, so calculate wisely to maximize your profits!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_COOKING_00: If I'm going to stay out exploring for a long time, I need a proper meal first! Maybe I should cook something with the ingredients we just got from that expedition.
Ugh... that smell coming from the pot is incredibly suspicious. You are checking your Cooking skill level before tossing ingredients in there, right?
W-what are you talking about?! If I take the time to cook it properly, it restores health and even gives permanent stat buffs!
R-right... in theory, maybe. But that purple smoke rising from the pot looks a lot more like poison potion fumes to me...
Heh, if you're that suspicious, then I'll gladly let you have the honor of being the first one to taste it, Bibi!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_CRAFTING_0: I've gathered quite a lot of wood and stone, but they're way too crude to just swing at monsters with like this. Can't I make some proper tools out of them?
Of course you can! With the Crafting skill, you can spend time making all kinds of equipment, weapons, and accessories yourself—not to mention consumables like arrows and mana stones.
Wow, so that means I can fully supply my own arrows and mana stones for ranged attacks and magic too?
Exactly. It's a crucial foundational skill that lets you turn basic materials into useful items essential for your survival.
Heh, just thinking about teaching monsters a lesson with equipment I carved and shaped with my own hands is already getting me excited!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_ENCHANTING: This sword feels a little dull after using it for so long. If I'm going to hunt monsters, I need it to hit harder.
In that case, why not spend some time enchanting your equipment with magical power? It can raise the gear's base stats by quite a lot.
Oh! So instead of finding a brand-new weapon, I can keep upgrading the gear I'm already using and push its stats much higher?
Exactly. But this delicate work takes concentration. If you fail, you'll lose your hard-earned materials, and there's a small chance the enchantment itself will weaken. So be careful!
Heh, time to show off my incredible concentration! Once I succeed, I'll sweep the hunting grounds clean with my massively boosted gear.
Why not practice enchanting stones before you try it on your equipment? Guiding the magic so it settles within the stone is what we call Mana Attunement.
Stones? So if it works, even an ordinary rock can become a magical stone?

That's right. If the magic takes hold, it becomes a Runestone. But if the attunement fails and you scorch the stone, all you'll have left is Coal. Better to get a feel for it before trying it on your favorite sword, wouldn't you say?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_EXPEDITION: Bibi, is there a way to re-explore areas that have already been made safe? I need more resources for cooking and crafting.
In that case, you can just use the expedition system. You can start from 2 stars, and the expedition time will vary depending on how many stars you got when you cleared the area.
Ah, so if I got a perfect 3-star clear, I can gather resources there much faster and more safely?
That's right. A wonderfully convenient life skill that keeps collecting resources for you while you're off goofing around doing something else.
H-hey, what do you mean goofing around? I'm busy all the time in my own way!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_FAMILIARTR: Bibi! I got a small, adorable companion while gathering materials by chance! Apparently, you can obtain one at a certain probability while using skills.
Oh? You already found yourself a decent familiar? Lucky you. But it's still too weak to be much help right away.
Hmm, then what do I need to do to make this little one stronger so it can help me on my adventures?
Spend some time training your companion with the Familiar Training skill. The more you train it, the higher its level becomes, and it'll start granting you very useful passive buffs.
Heh, then I guess I'd better put it through some intense training so it can make my life easier!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_FARMING_00: I'm exhausted... Every time I cook or make potions, I have to run all over the fields picking up ingredients again.
That's why smart adventurers make use of the Farming skill. Just plant seeds in your field and wait patiently.
Oh! So once I build up a proper farm, resources start coming in automatically without me having to run around collecting everything myself!
That's right. It takes time before the crops are ready to harvest, but for a steady supply of food and potion materials, it's absolutely essential.
And my overall stats go up permanently as my Farming level rises too? Then I need to start tilling the fields right away!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_INSTRUMENT: All this nonstop hunting and facing monsters has left me feeling emotionally drained. It feels like the sensitivity inside me is drying up and cracking...
In that case, take some time to use the Instrument Performance skill. Play a beautiful melody, soothe your cluttered mind, and gain fresh inspiration.
Wow, playing an instrument calms me down and even gives stat buffs! But what is this 'Inspiration' point I keep building up while I play used for?
That Inspiration is incredibly useful if you save it up. Later on, when you use other artistic skills like painting or writing, it can greatly improve the results.
So the inspiration I gain from music can create synergy with other art skills too? Then I need to take out an instrument and play a piece right now!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_INVENTORY_: Bibi, how do I use 'Category Settings'? I have so much stuff that my bag feels more like a small archive than a bag now.
You can create up to seven categories. Just pick the item types for each one and choose a marker color so the tabs are easy to recognize at a glance.
What happens if a category has more than thirty items? Do they get pushed into some unknown tab?

In that case, additional tabs with the same number and color will be created to continue the list. Items that don't fit into any category go to the normal tabs at the back, so you don't have to worry about anything disappearing.
Then what do the checkmarks and X marks on the color buttons mean?

The checkmark indicates the color of the category you're currently editing, and the X means that color is already in use by another category. Oh, and keep in mind that locked items are shown first within their respective tabs.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MEDITATION: I've been running around so much that my head feels cluttered... I need to sit still and meditate for a while.
A Meditation skill that empties your mind over time is a huge help for long-term growth.
So just sitting there quietly gives bonus effects to my other skills too?
Of course! It sharpens your focus, improves the efficiency of all your actions, and every time you meditate, your fundamentals grow stronger too.
Then whenever I get worn out from exploring or crafting, I should calm my mind with meditation and collect those bonuses bit by bit.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_001: Bibi, the Museum is open, but... it feels way too fancy for all the random junk in my bag. Do I just bring everything here one by one?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_002: You don't have to bring it all at once. Think of it as a gallery that records your journey. It also has a feature that shows you every item you've ever found.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_003: So the dark ones are things I haven't seen yet, and the faded ones are items I know about but haven't donated yet?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_004: Exactly. Just tap one to see more info. If you have a spare in your inventory, you can submit just one copy.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_005: A spare, huh... You'd better not be "borrowing" my favorite gear or anything I've locked!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_006: Relax. It won't touch locked stacks or equipped items. If you have multiples of the same item, it'll use the one with the lowest enhancement level first.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_007: Fine. Now, what about "Auto Submit"? It sounds convenient, but almost... too convenient. A little suspicious, don't you think?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_008: It only picks items that are safe to register, either from the current category or all of them. You'll get Milestone bonuses based on your total submissions; item rewards are claimed manually, but stat bonuses apply instantly.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_009: So once I've donated something, can I ask the museum to sell any new copies for me? My bag keeps filling up.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_MUSEUM_010: Of course. Tap a donated item and turn on Auto Sell. New copies you obtain will be converted into Gold at the current sell price, and you can turn it off from the same menu whenever you want.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_OBJECTIVES: Iris, don't tell me you're just going to wander around with no plan at all. Story quests—including the tutorial—are waiting for you.
Hmm... I thought I could just roam around and kill monsters. What's so good about clearing these objectives?
Well, for one, new skills unlock as you progress! And every now and then, random quests give you a nice little bonus of gold or items too.
Really? Then instead of mindlessly grinding, I should carefully check what quests are available first!
Exactly. The first step toward efficient growth is knowing exactly what you should be doing right now.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_PAINTING_0: The scenery out here is beautiful. It feels like such a waste to just pass by it—maybe I should take out a canvas and paint it.
Great idea! If you use the Painting skill to capture landscapes or people on canvas, it can earn you a pretty nice amount of gold.
Really? You mean paintings I spend time creating can actually sell for a high price? And they raise art-related stats too? That's amazing!
Correct! Well-crafted paintings are highly collectible and grant bonuses based on how often you paint them. Pick up your brush whenever you're free!
Heh, I'm going to paint masterpiece after masterpiece as the great artist Iris and rake in money by the armful!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_001_: Bibi, my life action queue is getting long. Am I just piling work on my future self?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_002_: Think of it as a handy to-do list. Once you line up your tasks now, the queue will handle them one by one in order—even while you are busy with other things or taking a rest. All you have to do is check the results later.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_003_: Oh, neat! So even if I ask for the same job many times, it won't just fill up the queue list with the exact same row over and over?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_004_: Right. Repeated work is kept as a planned count. The queue total tells you how much work is waiting, and the type count tells you how many different kinds of work are in the list.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_005_: What happens when one of them gets stuck? Like when I run out of materials, or my bag is full?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_006_: Then the queue sets that task aside for a moment and looks for another task you can do. If every task is stuck, it waits until you fix the reason.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_007_: And what about the 'estimated finish time'? Knowing when the list might calm down would really let me relax.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_QUEUE_008_: Treat it like a lantern, not a promise. Buffs may fade, new materials may arrive, and blocked tasks may wake up again. The time will keep updating as the queue changes.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_REST_001_T: Aah... after cooking, farming, and hunting, I don't even want to move anymore. I just want to stop doing everything and rest for a while.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_REST_002_T: That's fine. Sometimes you need Rest too—the kind where you stop everything and truly take a break. Even time spent doing nothing becomes part of your growth.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_REST_003_T: Huh? How does just breathing and lazing around help me grow?
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_REST_004_T: Because once your body has fully recovered, you receive a powerful buff that greatly increases the speed of all your life actions for a certain amount of time.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_REST_005_T: Oh, I get it! Instead of working myself to the bone nonstop, it's way more efficient to rest deeply first and then make a big push with that speed buff afterward.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_SMITHING_0: I mined some sturdy ore from the mines, but regular item crafting alone isn't enough to handle it.
That's because you need the specialized Smithing skill to work metal. You have to melt the ore down in intense heat and hammer it into shape.
Ah, so with Smithing, I can refine raw minerals and turn them into tougher, stronger metal-based equipment?
Exactly. If you want solid armor or sharp metal weapons, you can't afford to resent the time you spend sweating over the forge.
Ugh... hammering away in front of a blazing furnace sounds hot and exhausting, but if it's for my own safety, I'd better get to work.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_STEALTH_00: Bibi, see that merchant over there...? Don't you think I could sneak over and lift their coin pouch without them noticing?
Hm, if you want to pull it off before they notice, it'll take a fair amount of finesse. And if you get caught, it could end very badly for you.
Oh, come on, you know how nimble my hands are! If I succeed, I can get money and rare materials you normally can't obtain so easily.
Putting your hands on other people's belongings... If greed gets you caught and the guards chew you out, don't expect any sympathy from me.
Relax. If I move slowly enough and keep perfectly quiet, they'll just think it was a passing breeze.
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_TRAINING_0: Iris, if you want to take on stronger monsters, you can't just keep swinging wildly. It's time to build real survivability through Training.
Training? You mean some ordinary routine that just raises basic stats like health or defense a little?

Heh, shows what you know! If you train consistently, you can learn action skills you can use yourself during hunts with precise timing—things like dodging a deadly attack in a flash or recovering your own health in a crisis.
Oh! So it's not just about boosting stats—I can actually cast defensive buffs myself or use evasive moves to barely scrape through alive!
Exactly! And the higher your Training level gets, the shorter those action skill cooldowns become, and the more they heal too. So if you want to last longer in the field, never slack off on training!
Dialogue/DIALOGUE_GUIDES_LIFE_WRITING_00: I want to organize everything that happened on today's exploration... I wonder if there is any paper left in my bag?
Check the corner of your bag. You can use the Writing skill to record diaries, novels, or research notes. Putting your experiences into words provides a special boost to your growth.
Just writing on paper with a pen helps me grow? How does that work exactly?

A drama increases the Action Speed of the skills used as material, and a poetry collection pours a large amount of EXP into a selected skill upon completion. It is a way to practically improve your stats through recording.
I see! So I collect the time I spent working and turn it back into growth. That is way more practical than I expected for an art!
Note that actions that take too long to perform are not used as writing material. It is hard to stay focused on writing if a single task drags on forever, so those topics are excluded.
I see. But I wonder if I can keep writing poetry collections... To be honest, my concentration isn't exactly my strongest suit.

That is why a poetry collection automatically switches to the next theme once you finish a book. Writing about the same topic for too long can kill your focus, so it switches to help you find fresh inspiration and stay engaged in your work.

Enemy/0006C_Name: Bellkeeper of the Funeral Sea Mist
Item/CMPM0006_Desc: A pine cone with a mysterious purple glow. It is Pori’s most treasured item; instead of eating them, Pori loves to collect and keep them safe.
Item/COMPOST0001_Desc: A simple compost for vegetables, fruit, herbs and trees.
Item/COMPOST0002_Desc: Nutrient-rich compost that increases the main crop yield.
Item/COMPOST0003_Desc: Compost that slowly nourishes roots, increasing crop yield at the cost of a longer growing period.
Item/COMPOST0004_Desc: Compost that promotes growth so crops can be harvested sooner.
Item/FU0007_Desc: "Academia classifies it as a fruit! Why won't the chefs listen?"
Item/POE0001_Desc: A potion that increases XP gained in Endurance, Melee, Ranged, and Magic.
Item/POE0002_Desc: A potion that increases XP gained in all life skills, including Mining, Logging, and Fishing.
Item/POE0003_Desc: A potion that increases XP gained in Endurance, Melee, Ranged, and Magic.
Item/POE0004_Desc: A potion that increases XP gained in all life skills, including Mining, Logging, and Fishing.
Item/POE0005_Desc: A potion that increases XP gained in Endurance, Melee, Ranged, and Magic.
Item/POE0006_Desc: A potion that increases XP gained in all life skills, including Mining, Logging, and Fishing.
Item/SPECHAL0001_Desc: Saves time, as long as you don't count the time spent winding it every day.
Item/SPECHAL0002_Desc: Rings precisely every hour. It won't make an exception even for the break of dawn.
Item/SPECHAL0003_Desc: After a swing, it snaps back to its original position. Unfortunately, your wrist goes with it.
Item/SPECHAL0004_Desc: Arrows orbit the enemy seeking a blind spot. Sometimes they orbit the owner instead.
Item/SPECHAL0005_Desc: Spells strengthen as the sand flows upward. Turning it over doesn't change the direction.
Item/SPECHAL0006_Desc: Unwinds a thread leading to the exit. Occasionally it wraps around the wearer first.
Item/SPECHAL0007_Desc: Changes shape whenever the labyrinth walls move. It doesn't care about your finger size.
Item/SPECHAL0008_Desc: Severs the threads of tangled fate. It’s remarkably useless against ordinary string.
Item/SPECHAL0009_Desc: A missed arrow retraces its path. Returning, however, doesn't guarantee a hit.
Item/SPECHAL0010_Desc: Winds spells like thread to be cast again. It also repeats your stumbles perfectly.
Item/SPECHAL0011_Desc: Retrace your exact steps, footprints and all. Sometimes they trigger after you've arrived.
Item/SPECHAL0012_Desc: Winds back local time with every turn. Be careful when tightening any screws.
Item/SPECHAL0013_Desc: The brim completes a full turn at noon. More useful for others to check the time than you.
Item/SPECOMB0001_Desc: Emits phytoncide when hitting. Might actually make the enemy healthier.
Item/SPECOMB0002_Desc: Thought it was a diamond ring? It's just a round-carved pebble.
Item/SPECOMB0003_Desc: Improves jump height, but it's incredibly hard to lift your feet off the floor.
Item/SPECOMB0004_Desc: Never lets go of a grabbed collar. The problem is it won't let go of your hands either.
Item/SPECOMB0005_Desc: Makes a majestic bell sound when blocking. Feels like your eardrums will burst.
Item/SPECOMB0006_Desc: A hug turns both you and the enemy into a well-done steak.
Item/SPECOMB0007_Desc: Stand still and you'll literally take root in the ground. Beware of immobilization.
Item/SPECOMB0008_Desc: A bone helm perfect for being teased about having an empty head.
Item/SPECOMB0009_Desc: A legendary sword that cleaves the cosmos! Currently used mostly for peeling fruit.
Item/SPECOMB0010_Desc: So heavy that wearing it lets you experience the water pressure of 10,000 meters deep.
Item/SPECOMB0011_Desc: Covered in burrs and ticks from running through bushes. Too itchy to stand still.
Item/SPECOMB0012_Desc: Your fingers bleed every time you draw the string. Gloves are absolutely mandatory.
Item/SPECOMB0013_Desc: Vision splits into 100. It's confusing whether you're actually aiming well or not.
Item/SPECOMB0014_Desc: Fly forward with a tailwind, forcefully moonwalk with a headwind.
Item/SPECOMB0015_Desc: The cruel hunting method of rubbing salt in the wound! Extra umami is a bonus.
Item/SPECOMB0016_Desc: Great because the bowstring doesn't chafe your chest. Just endure the smell.
Item/SPECOMB0017_Desc: Feels like tentacles sprouted on your drawing fingers. It feels extremely gross.
Item/SPECOMB0018_Desc: A miraculous(?) accessory that increases accuracy when you shoot with eyes closed.
Item/SPECOMB0019_Desc: Blends perfectly into the dark. Even allies can't see you and will step on you.
Item/SPECOMB0020_Desc: Shoots miniature black holes instead of arrows. Feels like my arm is getting sucked in whenever I draw the string.
Item/SPECOMB0021_Desc: The more mana you focus, the saltier it smells. Don't lick it out of curiosity.
Item/SPECOMB0022_Desc: Pokes your finger whenever mana regens. Pain is a great source of magic.
Item/SPECOMB0023_Desc: Wave elegantly to shoot destructive magic. Way too heavy for a baton.
Item/SPECOMB0024_Desc: Ink drips from your hands when casting. Careful when reading your grimoire.
Item/SPECOMB0025_Desc: Wizards look mysterious because they are holding back coughs inside this hood.
Item/SPECOMB0026_Desc: Keeps your butt constantly warm. Might be excellent for winter and hemorrhoid prevention.
Item/SPECOMB0027_Desc: Imbued with cursed mana. Your fashion sense is cursed along with it.
Item/SPECOMB0028_Desc: You occasionally hear mysterious whispers. Sounds like they're asking if you've eaten.
Item/SPECOMB0029_Desc: Wearing it makes you forget why you walked into a room. True oblivion.
Item/SPECOMB0030_Desc: The tooth is so huge it's more a blunt weapon than a staff. This is Magic (Physical).
Item/SPECOMB0031_Desc: A heavy axe that splits firewood and monster skulls with equal ease.
Item/SPECOMB0032_Desc: Powerful bow made from tent poles. Its only flaw is that you now have nowhere to sleep.
Item/SPECOMB0033_Desc: A lantern for the camp and a kerosene flamethrower for your enemies.
Item/SPECOMB0034_Desc: The roots dig so deep you have to lift the whole patch of soil to move.
Item/SPECOMB0035_Desc: One swing drags you to the end of the skyrail. Worry about the wall, not the enemy.
Item/SPECOMB0036_Desc: Enemy weapons stick to the chestplate. The catch? Your own weapon gets stuck too.
Item/SPECOMB0037_Desc: The pockets never end. You find long-lost items before retrieving what you stole.
Item/SPECOMB0038_Desc: Rewinds time when you miss. But your embarrassed face remains permanently recorded.
Item/SPECOMB0039_Desc: Points straight to the most valuable treasure. Sadly, enemies are usually in the opposite direction.
Item/SPECOMB0040_Desc: Automatically pulls fired arrows and tent pegs back to your boots. Hope your insteps survive.
Item/SPECOMB0041_Desc: Forces you to shoot on the beat. Miss it, and the gloves will snap your fingers.
Item/SPECOMB0042_Desc: Rewinds one stroke when you botch a spell. Fail repeatedly, and the growth rings sigh.
Item/SPECOMB0043_Desc: Reflects enemy magic. It also vividly reflects the terrified faces of your allies.
Item/SPECOMB0044_Desc: Neatly aligns metal pieces. Watch out for dinner spoons joining the queue.
Item/SPECOMB0045_Desc: Soles stay clean through any paint, but your entire path becomes a colorful masterpiece.
Item/SPENONC0001_Desc: You only find the true path once you're lost. Not the path home, obviously.
Item/SPENONC0002_Desc: The perfect sole angle, crafted by thousands of retreats.
Item/SPENONC0003_Desc: Great for navigating at night. Also great for telling enemies exactly where you are.
Item/SPENONC0004_Desc: Getting hit by this doesn't hurt, it just makes you hungry.
Item/SPENONC0005_Desc: Chefs don't cry. Their eyes just sweat.
Item/SPENONC0006_Desc: The food is burnt to a crisp, but the apron is spotless.
Item/SPENONC0007_Desc: Makes you feel like you just did 500 squats. Smells like it too.
Item/SPENONC0008_Desc: You feel like you could fly after taking them off, but your knees just hurt.
Item/SPENONC0009_Desc: You hear phantom whispers of "One more rep!" Please stop.
Item/SPENONC0010_Desc: Seeds automatically plant themselves into the dirt. Sometimes into your feet, too.
Item/SPENONC0011_Desc: Crows fly over to be your friend. Not very helpful for the harvest.
Item/SPENONC0012_Desc: The water never runs out, but it's too heavy to lift.
Item/SPENONC0013_Desc: Completely eliminates footsteps. Except for the hole at the big toe.
Item/SPENONC0014_Desc: Only the cloak turns invisible. Your body is still perfectly visible.
Item/SPENONC0015_Desc: Tell the lock it looks pretty and it opens. You have to mean it.
Item/SPENONC0016_Desc: Strawberry flavor or poison? Life is a gamble.
Item/SPENONC0017_Desc: Protects your skin (and only your skin) from exploding potions.
Item/SPENONC0018_Desc: Cures shaky hands perfectly. You shake twice as much when you take them off.
Item/SPENONC0019_Desc: Floats about 1cm off the ground. Great for lower back pain.
Item/SPENONC0020_Desc: What's for dinner? That thought is the ring's fault.
Item/SPENONC0021_Desc: Everything looks like runic text. The downside is you become illiterate.
Item/SPENONC0022_Desc: One touch makes your gear stronger, or turns it to dust.
Item/SPENONC0023_Desc: A miraculous necklace that makes 99% success rates fail. Could the opposite be true?
Item/SPENONC0024_Desc: It has every tool imaginable. It just takes 3 hours to find them.
Item/SPENONC0025_Desc: Hammered so much that the gloves themselves became a hammer.
Item/SPENONC0026_Desc: Helps with micro-crafting. Beware of fires under sunlight.
Item/SPENONC0027_Desc: Impervious to stepping in lava, but can't withstand foot odor.
Item/SPENONC0028_Desc: A crystallized drop of sweat. A bit gross, honestly.
Item/SPENONC0029_Desc: You can't hear the hammering, but you also can't hear monster footsteps.
Item/SPENONC0030_Desc: The ink overflows and covers the map in black. Rely on your memory.
Item/SPENONC0031_Desc: It always points North. But you don't know where North is.
Item/SPENONC0032_Desc: Makes even monsters wag their tails. It tastes good when I eat it too.
Item/SPENONC0033_Desc: Makes you feel like the king of beasts. Until a stray cat hisses at you.
Item/SPENONC0034_Desc: Squeaks when pressed. Draws aggro from every monster.
Item/SPENONC0035_Desc: Makes a mournful sound. Or maybe it's just air leaking.
Item/SPENONC0036_Desc: All eyes on you! People care more about the hat than your playing.
Item/SPENONC0037_Desc: The colors dance. Enemies run away in confusion.
Item/SPENONC0038_Desc: Wearing it makes you feel like speaking French. Je t'aime?
Item/SPENONC0039_Desc: The crystallization of an artistic soul that gave up on laundry.
Item/SPENONC0040_Desc: Every typo in the world appears in red. Causes extreme headaches.
Item/SPENONC0041_Desc: The ticking raises your heart rate, forcing your writing speed up.
Item/SPENONC0042_Desc: Forces a smiling face to boost negotiation. Your jaw hurts.
Item/SPENONC0043_Desc: Hands move faster during trades. If caught, say goodbye to your wrists.
Item/SPENONC0044_Desc: There's so much money it won't open. You can't even spend it.
Item/SPENONC0045_Desc: Blocks biting winds, but traps sweat and odor until allies pass out.
Item/SPENONC0046_Desc: Endless pockets hold all your gear. Warning: too much weight leads to a pants drop.
Item/SPENONC0047_Desc: They do everything for your survival. Except let you take them off.
Item/SPENONC0048_Desc: Seeds keep rolling out of the deep pocket. Best not to ask where they come from.
Item/SPENONC0049_Desc: Conceals your face perfectly. Unfortunately, "LEGENDARY THIEF" is written across the forehead in gold.

Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_001: Check your objectives, then add smelting tasks to the queue to craft copper ingots and copper daggers.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_002: Equip the copper dagger you just crafted from your inventory and check your current equipment status on the equipment screen.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_003: Take your copper dagger and challenge the Sunny Bushland again to clear your first exploration area.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_004: Enter the mining gathering area, break ore veins, and learn the flow of obtaining metal materials.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_005: Enter the forest gathering area and see how to obtain wood and plant-based materials.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_006: Complete the ocean gathering area to obtain seafood materials and prepare to unlock the next growth path: Cooking.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_007: Use the Cooking skill to turn ingredients into food and learn about the recovery effects provided by food.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_008: Equip the completed food and check the support effects applied to exploration.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_009: Proceed with training to grow your action skills and try switching the actions used in exploration.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_010: Re-challenge the Sunlit Grove and unleash action skills without restraint.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_011: Move stealthily and use the Thievery skill to target rewards that are difficult to obtain through normal exploration or gathering.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_012: Farming is not a task that repeats immediately in a queue; it is a long-term production system where you plant seeds or give instructions to livestock and harvest after time passes.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_013: Craft various potions that help with exploration and life activities through Potion Making.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_014: Learn how to turn basic materials into equipment, accessories, and consumables using the Crafting skill.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_015: Learn how to record regions and open new routes with Cartography, as well as the repeat bonuses after unlocking.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_016: Check the flow of automatically gathering resources by sending expeditions back to areas you've already cleared.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_017: Lay the foundation for long-term growth bonuses and increased action efficiency through Meditation.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_018: Train familiars to gain passive buffs for your adventures. Familiars unlock as you progress through other skills, and can be trained once unlocked.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_019: Gain inspiration through playing musical instruments and see how this inspiration serves as a resource to improve the performance of other artistic activities.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_020: Paint to create sellable artworks and learn the growth and achievement flow of the arts category.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_021: Check the growth structure that leads to random skill missions, action speed bonuses, and experience rewards through Writing.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_022: Learn the flow of item sales efficiency and special currency exchange with the Commerce skill to secure adventure funds reliably.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_023: Check the Enchantment system, which boosts performance by infusing equipment with magic, and the concept of success probability.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_024: Learn how Rest buffs improve life action speeds. After unlocking Rest, it will begin automatically when the queue stays inactive for a while.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_025: Give an Oak Acorn to Pori.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_026: Start camping as Pori taught you.
Objectives/OBJECTIVES_MAINOBJECTIVES_027: Craft Travel Rations to prepare for the next camp and receive a Purple Pine Cone, Pori's favorite.
Painting/UI_PAINTING_MILESTONE_CURRENT_B: Increases the chance to get double painting rewards.
Reduces the time needed to finish one painting action.
Increases the Painting skill EXP earned per completion.
Painting/UI_PAINTING_MILESTONE_PROGRESS_: Bonus activates only when both kill/clear count and painting count pass the threshold.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_34:
Combat / Familiars

- Changed combat familiar unlock mechanics.
- Fixed an issue where the unlock chance was much lower than intended.

Camping / Objectives

- Updated Camping skill and main objectives.

Crafting

- Fixed Magic Armor subcategory order in Crafting.

Dialogue / UI

- Adjusted dialogue page text limits by language.
- Fixed some Farming scroll view clipping issues.

Auto Explore / Performance

- Simplified Auto Explore item reward popups.
- Reduced lag caused by reward popups.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_35:
Language Addition

- Spanish language support has been added.

Rest / Familiars

- Increased the unlock chance for Rest-related familiars.

Gold Shop

- Reduced the price scaling for Inventory Expansion Tickets in the Gold Shop.
- Before: x1.4 every 5 purchases
- After: x1.2 every 5 purchases

Crafting / Smithing

- Increased the EXP gained from Crafting and Smithing items that consume more of the same material.
- Adjusted crafting actions that use more materials so their EXP gain is reflected more naturally.

Stealth

- Adjusted early Stealth balance.
- Adjusted action times for actions with the same EXP but different required levels.

Writing

- Fixed the max queue count display issue for Writing (Drama).
- Before: 3000
- After: 1

Patch Notes

- Patch notes can now be viewed in game.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_36:
Google Play Games

- Improved excessive Google Play Games re-login attempts.

Actions

- Added actions for Leap and Combat Mastery.
- Leap: leaps forward toward the enemy.
- Combat Mastery: increases attack speed by reducing Attack Interval.

Sale Confirmation

- Sale price is now shown again on the sale confirmation screen.

Exploration

- Equipped items are now also checked for consumption requirements during Exploration.

Inventory

- Added the option to drink potions from the Inventory.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_37:
Familiars / Exploration

- Fixed an issue where Exploration familiars were not applying critical chance.

Potions

- Added sound and popup effects when potions are used automatically.

Commerce

- Added Commodity Trade to the Commerce skill.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_38:
Ducarin Shop

- Updated the Ducarin Shop description.
- Clarified Commerce skills: Special Exchange and Commodity Trade.

Data Loading

- Added data load validation when starting the game.
- Fixed issues caused by incorrect data loading.

Items

- Separated plant tomatoes / fruit tomatoes and their seeds, and added descriptions.
- Added detailed views for item source and usage information.
- Fixed an issue where item materials were not refreshing properly.

Objectives

- Relaxed the clear condition for Skill Expansion 7 (Rest).

Settings

- Added a setting to show or hide item acquisition popups.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_39:
Queue

- Holding a queue button can now move it to the top or bottom.

Potions

- Potion popups now show whether the same potion buff is already active.

Skill Locks

- Fixed an issue where some skill lock windows could temporarily unlock while the skill was still locked.

Exploration

- EXP gained can now be checked when Exploration is completed.

UI / Text

- Added outlines to some text to improve readability.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_40:
Potion Name

- Updated the Creativity Potion name to sound more natural.

Item Info

- Item Info now shows owned quantity.

Inventory

- Added inventory categories and related explanations.

Sound Effects

- Added sound effects for toggle buttons.

Offline Progress

- Fixed display issues in the offline progress summary.
- Fixed an issue where the Life window sometimes did not appear.
- Fixed an Expedition EXP display issue.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_41:
Item Info

- Improved the detailed view format for item sources and uses.
- Added images and adjusted the UI layout.

Painting / Farming

- Fixed some incorrect images in Painting.
- Fixed some incorrect names in Farming.

Skills

- Actions within each skill are now sorted primarily by their skill level requirements.

Commerce

- Fixed an issue where the Commerce button could become disabled.

Character Appearance

- Updated the hero's colors during Exploration to match the original illustration.
- Updated the hero's appearance in some Life skills to match the original illustration.

Inventory

- Added a warning when changing equipment while the Inventory is full.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_42:
Challenge

- Added Challenge content: Trial Tower, Rewinding Labyrinth, and Challenge Shop.
- Available at Endurance Lv. 15 or higher.

Skills

- Level caps for all skills can now be raised with tickets from the Challenge Shop.
- Additional actions for higher skill levels will be added in future updates.

Item Info

- Added the maximum slot counts to the descriptions of Loadout Slot Tickets and Reward Slot Tickets.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_43:
Challenge

- Fixed equipment and loadout change issues in Challenge content.
- Fixed issues where equipment effects were not applied or items could be deleted or duplicated.

Exploration

- Fixed an issue where equipped items could occasionally become invisible during Exploration.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_44:
Potions

- Fixed an issue where potions were not consumed automatically after changing equipment.

Writing

- Skills that have not been unlocked are now excluded from Writing candidates.

Enchanting

- Fixed an issue where the material-saving chance was not applied during Enchanting.

Stealth / Meditation

- Fixed an issue where some data was not refreshed after ranking up Stealth or Meditation.

Combat

- Fixed an issue where ranged attacks could occasionally hit more than one enemy.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_45:
Language

- Added Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese support.

Ducarin Shop

- Reduced the prices of some items in the Ducarin Shop.

Commerce

- Improved Commodity Trade in the Commerce Life skill.
- Separated buying and selling.
- Adjusted Ducarin price balance.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_46:
Combat Balance

- Increased the attack power of arrows and mana stones.

Chests

- Item drop rates in chests are now displayed to two decimal places.
- Adjusted the drop rates of some chest items.
- Corrected rewards that could require more than 10 inventory slots because their drop rates were below 100%.

Content Expansion

- Added exploration areas and items up to level 120.
- Added actions up to level 120 for most skills, greatly expanding the available content.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_47:
Exploration

- Changed the target location image displayed during Exploration.
- Fixed an issue where the abandon button and camera lock were linked during Exploration.

Cartography

- Fixed an issue where the wrong queue image was displayed after level 100.

Farming

- Fixed a slight discrepancy between reaching 100% progress and crops becoming available to harvest.

Training

- Swapped the stats of two special Training items (Speed and Experience Multiplier).
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_48:
Queue

- Fixed an issue where clicking a queued icon for Painting and some other skills did not navigate to the correct action.
- Fixed an issue where required materials and currency were not shown for some queued actions.
- Actions can now be added to the queue even without enough materials or currency. If they are still insufficient when the action's turn arrives, it will wait until enough are available.

Localization

- Localized the game logo for each supported language.

Enchanting

- Increased Enchanting mastery and EXP gains.
- Fixed issues with the Enchanting queue.

Potions

- Improved automatic potion use so each potion is consumed only when its effects can actually apply.

Commerce

- Fixed item prices wrapping onto another line when the values grew longer.

Camping

- Reduced the load caused by Camping during offline progress simulation.

Inventory

- Added a “Use All” button for Inventory Slot Tickets.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_49:
Tutorial

- Improved the tutorial guide so it points to the correct target more accurately.

Combat

- Increased the hero's base HP at level 1 from 20 to 25.

Challenge

- Added five new Challenge bosses.

Commerce

- When Masterpiece Appraisal or Special Exchange reaches rank S or higher, you can now jump directly to that Commerce action from the item sale window.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_50:
Exploration

- Added an arrow button to collapse or expand active buff icons.
- Added a Levels tab to the stats panel where you can view levels and EXP for Exploration-related skills.

Museum

- Added Auto Sell for donated items. When enabled in the Museum, newly acquired copies are automatically sold for Gold.

Challenge

- Fixed an issue where Challenge currency rewards were not clearly displayed in the Clear Bonus section after completion.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_51:
Equipment

- Fixed an issue where some items could not be equipped even when their requirements were met.

Farming

- The Farming button now glows green when crops are ready to harvest.
- Moved the Farming button higher in the Action window.
- Increased herb harvest yields and added more ways to obtain some herbs.
- Increased both growth times and corresponding rewards by 2–6 times, depending on the crop, to make harvesting more convenient.

Mining

- Increased the amounts of Stone and Coal obtained from mines.

Enchanting

- Added Mana Attunement, a new Enchanting action.

Painting

- Doubled Painting rank EXP gains and increased the prices of perfectly painted works.

Smelting / Cooking

- Reduced Coal requirements for Smelting.
- Corrected the calculation for Coal rewards from failed Cooking attempts so the 95% success / 5% failure probabilities are applied correctly.

Gold Shop / Commerce

- Rebalanced Gold Shop prices and added a cap on price increases.
- Commerce skill shortcuts are now available when selling a single item.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_52:
Challenge / Combat

- Added a screen transition when clearing a Challenge.
- Fixed an issue where advancing or retreating during an action in a Challenge reset its cooldown.
- Adjusted the levels of some dungeon and regular monsters so dungeon bosses have higher levels.

Purchase / Offline Play

- Players who have purchased the game can now play the purchased version without an internet connection.

Equipment / Enchanting

- Improved data for some equipment whose stats did not change when enchanted.
- Fixed the display and application of Life Action Speed enchantment effects.

Instrument Performance

- Improved the Instrument Performance UI and rewards.

Potions

- Added descriptions for experience potions.

Crafting

- Adjusted level requirements for crafted items.

Auto Exploration / Expedition

- Familiars can now also be unlocked through Auto Exploration and Expeditions.

Commerce

- Fixed an issue where Commerce progress stopped during offline simulation.

Museum / Inventory

- Improved item classification and sorting by type in the Museum and Inventory.

Saving / Performance

- Improved saving and reduced system load.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_53:
Training

- New traits can now be selected for existing Training actions upon reaching SSS rank.

Terminology (English Only)

- Renamed "Idle Action Speed" to "Life Action Speed" in the English text only. The wording in other languages remains unchanged.

Farming

- Added four types of compost for use in Farming.
PatchNotes/PATCH_NOTES_BODY_0_54:
Farming

- Failed results are now shown first when starting all Farming activities, and a results summary has been added.
- Livestock Pens now occasionally yield compost.

Skill/Brewing_Desc: Brew exploration potions and life potions from gathered materials. Potions can improve combat stats or speed up specific life skills.
Skill/Camping_Desc: Prepare supplies and set up camp to support other life skills with temporary EXP bonuses.
Skill/Cartography_Desc: Chart regional maps to unlock new destinations. Successfully charting a map opens up locked areas and grants a Cartography skill XP bonus for the unlocked map entry.
Skill/Combat_Endurance_Desc: Your endurance, tempered through exploration. Defeating monsters grants XP.
Skill/Combat_Magic_Desc: Represents your proficiency with magic weapons. Defeated monsters with magic weapons grant XP.
Skill/Combat_Melee_Desc: Represents your proficiency with melee weapons. Defeated monsters with melee weapons grant XP.
Skill/Combat_Ranged_Desc: Represents your proficiency with ranged weapons. Defeated monsters with ranged weapons grant XP.
Skill/Commerce_Desc: Trade items through Instant Liquidation, Masterpiece Appraisal, or Special Exchange. You can increase your payout from regular sales or exchange selected items for Gold or Ducarin, earning bonuses based on your action rank.
Skill/Cooking_Desc: Craft dishes using gathered ingredients. Finished meals can be equipped as consumables to aid your exploration or used as expedition materials.
Skill/Crafting_Desc: Craft equipment and utility items from gathered materials. Recipes include ranged armor, mage armor, arrows, mana stones, accessories, bows, magic weapons and charms.
Skill/Enchanting_Desc: Select a piece of equipment to attempt enchanting. Rates for success, failure (maintaining level), and critical failure (dropping level) vary depending on your action. Special materials can be used to boost the success rate or protect your enchanting level.
Skill/Expedition_Desc: Send expeditions to unlocked destinations to earn rewards. This feature is available only for destinations cleared with a 2-star rating or higher. If cleared with 3 stars, the expedition time will be shortened to meet the 3-star standard.
Skill/FamiliarTraining_Desc: Unlock and train familiars through skills attacks and objectives. Familiars provide bonuses including skill EXP action speed input conservation double output crit chance and objective reward doubling.
Skill/Farming_Desc: Run passive production slots for vegetables, fruit, herbs, livestock and wood. Farmed materials support Cooking, Brewing, Crafting and other life skills.
Skill/InstrumentPerformance_Desc: Perform instruments to earn Inspiration for Painting and Writing. You may also receive tips and, from some performances, items from the audience. Higher-tier instruments grant more Inspiration and larger tips.
Skill/Life_Fishing_Desc: Gather seafood and aquatic resources from Schools of fish. As your Fishing level increases, you can properly obtain the full rewards from higher-tier Schools of fish.
Skill/Life_Logging_Desc: Gather timber and forest resources from Wild trees. As your Logging level increases, you can properly obtain the full rewards from higher-tier Wild trees.
Skill/Life_Mining_Desc: Gather ore and mineral resources from Mining rocks. As your Mining level increases, you can properly obtain the full rewards from higher-tier Mining rocks.
Skill/Meditation_Desc: Complete meditation actions to build temporary speed buffs. Meditation can improve global skill speed, selected skill speed and combat stats.
Skill/Painting_Desc: Sketch areas and enemies. Reaching the target numbers for both sketches and kills/clears unlocks milestone bonuses, boosting action speed and the chance for double skill XP.
Skill/Rest_Desc: Rest to gain a temporary skill speed bonus. Auto Rest can repeat the action and keep the rest bonus active while resources allow.
Skill/Smithing_Desc: Smelt ore into ingots and craft metal equipment. Depending on the metal tier, you can craft armor, weapons, gathering tools, rings, and arrowheads.
Skill/Stealth_Desc: Select a target to perform a stealth action and claim rewards. Higher-level targets have a much lower success rate, but offer better loot. Failing a theft triggers a brief cooldown.
Skill/Training_Desc: Repeatedly practice combat actions to increase your mastery. Raising your rank enhances that specific action.
Skill/Writing_Desc: Spend Inspiration to write works such as Drama and Poetry. Writing can speed up assigned skills or grant EXP to random unlocked actions within an assigned skill.
Stats/STAT_ACCURACY_DESC: Higher Accuracy compared to the target's Evasion increases hit chance.
Stats/STAT_APPETITE_DESC: Reduces food cooldowns, up to 40% (minimum 60% of the base time).
Stats/STAT_ATTACK_INTERVAL_DESC: Player attack interval. (Reduced to 0.1s max) During gathering, weapon/armor/accessory effects are excluded; only gathering gear applies. (Skills and buffs can be applied)
Stats/STAT_ATTACK_RANGE_DESC: Distance from which you can attack enemies.
Stats/STAT_BOSS_DAMAGE_DESC: Increases damage dealt to Boss and Challenge Boss enemies.
Stats/STAT_CRIT_CHANCE_DESC: Chance to deal extra damage. Each 100% above 100% adds another +100% critical damage.
Stats/STAT_DAMAGE_REDUCTION_DESC: Percentage value that reduces incoming damage. It actually caps at 95%.
Stats/STAT_DEFENSE_DESC: Flat value that reduces incoming damage.
Stats/STAT_DEXTERITY_DESC: Affects stealth and other precision-based actions.
Stats/STAT_EVASION_DESC: Higher Evasion compared to the attacker's Accuracy increases dodge chance.
Stats/STAT_HP_REGEN_DESC: Amount of HP restored automatically once every 3 seconds.
Stats/STAT_IDLE_ACTION_INTERVAL_DESC: Speed multiplier for life actions. Higher values reduce the time needed to complete each action.
Stats/STAT_LUCK_DESC: Retries failed item rewards from exploration, area clear rewards, and expeditions. Gold is unaffected. Each 100% Luck adds 1 extra retry, and Luck is capped at 1000%.
Stats/STAT_MAX_DAMAGE_DESC: Maximum damage dealt when the target has no Defense.
Stats/STAT_MAX_HP_DESC: Maximum amount of HP you can have during exploration.
Stats/STAT_MIN_DAMAGE_DESC: Minimum damage dealt when the target has no Defense.
Stats/STAT_MOBILITY_DESC: Reduces action skill cooldowns, up to 40% (minimum 60% of the base time).
Stats/STAT_MOVE_SPEED_DESC: Speed at which the player moves.
Stats/STAT_SIGHT_DESC: Distance from which you can detect enemies.
UI/UI_CURRENCY_CYCLE_STONE_DESC: Currency earned from the Trial Tower.
UI/UI_CURRENCY_REWIND_THREAD_DESC: Currency earned from the Rewinding Labyrinth.
UI/UI_RESOURCE_INSPIRATION_DESC: Used for Painting and Writing actions.
Writing/UI_WRITING_ACTION1_OUTPUT_DESC_F: The 3 assigned skills run +{1}% faster for {0} minutes.
Writing/UI_WRITING_ACTION2_OUTPUT_DESC_F: Provides {0}x EXP for 1 random unlocked Action within the assigned skill.
Writing/UI_WRITING_BUFF_DRAMA_DESC_FORMA: The {2} skill progresses +{1}% faster for {0} minutes.
